resources.string: Shogi

Japanese chess. Tap one of your pieces (they point up), then a green dot. Pieces you capture join your side: tap one below the board to place it on an empty square. Checkmate the computer’s king to win.
Shogi (9 × 9)
The full game on the 9 by 9 board.
Mini shogi (5 × 5)
A small 5 by 5 board with fewer pieces: quick games, good for learning.
Your turn: tap one of your pieces, on the board or in your hand
Tap a green dot to move there
Tap a green dot to place the piece there
Check! Your king is attacked: protect it
Pieces
How the pieces move

On each piece, a dot is one step that way and an arrow means any distance. Red characters are promoted pieces. The shaded rows at the far side (three rows, one in mini shogi) are where your pieces can promote.
King (王, 玉): one step in any direction.
Rook (飛): any distance along a line. Promotes to a dragon.
Bishop (角): any distance diagonally. Promotes to a horse.
Gold general (金): one step in any direction except diagonally backward. It does not promote.
Silver general (銀): one step forward or diagonally. Promoted, it moves like a gold.
Knight (桂): jumps two forward and one to the side, over any piece. Promoted, it moves like a gold.
Lance (香): any distance straight forward. Promoted, it moves like a gold.
Pawn (歩): one step forward. Promoted, it becomes a tokin (と) and moves like a gold.
Dragon (龍), the promoted rook: any distance along a line, or one step diagonally.
Horse (馬), the promoted bishop: any distance diagonally, or one step along a line.
Promoted pawn, lance, knight or silver (と, 杏, 圭, 全): moves like a gold general.
